events.summary: We have updated the Last Civilization: Inherited Flame demo. You can now select 日本語, English, 简体中文, or Deutsch directly from the title screen using native-language labels. Your saved language choice takes priority. If no choice has been saved, the demo checks your Steam language, then your OS language, and falls back to English. events.title: Development diary: See your next move, from hearth repairs to timber deliveries
events.summary: A village worth protecting. A clearer next move. Morning arrives with a damaged hearth. Where should recovery begin? Timber has been cut, yet village stock is low. Two residents are tending one field, but one is labeled as waiting. We are working through these points of confusion found during actual play. events.title: Development diary: The people who keep the flame alive
events.summary: A night survived is a story of the people who worked through it. In Last Civilization: Inherited Flame, protecting the last flame should be more than watching a resource counter. Who brought the fuel? Who repaired a breach? Who needed to rest before taking another watch? Our latest work, on October 16–17, focuses on making those jobs function as intended and connect to residents' records. These are development-build changes. events.summary: Protect the flame. Get to know the people who keep it alive. In Last Civilization: Inherited Flame, a village is more than a collection of buildings. Preparing by day, protecting the flame by night and remembering each resident should connect into one story. Following our October 7 demo update, we have continued improving the development build. events.title: Demo update: Meet your residents and follow your village’s growing knowledge
events.summary: Seeing your village change makes the next choice more meaningful. We have updated the Last Civilization: Inherited Flame demo, focusing on readable information and clearer explanations for your decisions. Prepare by day, protect the flame by night, and keep the stories of your residents and village alive. If the amount of information left you unsure before, we invite you to revisit the first ten days. events.title: Preparing for Early Access - A Civilization's Story We Build Together
events.summary: We are preparing Last Civilization: Inherited Flame for Early Access. The heart of the game is not only building a village, but passing the records and choices of the people who lived there to the next civilization. The current full-game candidate offers daytime settlement management, gathering and construction, night defense, residents' life histories, and inheritance after a village falls, with long-term progression toward Day 100. events.title: Cave of Echoes - Searching for a Lost Village's Memories
events.summary: Beyond the village lie traces of people who once protected the flame. In Cave of Echoes, a feature in development for the full game, you choose residents and send them out with food and fuel for their light. Inside the cave, decide whether to push farther or return safely. Going deeper may uncover another clue, but an expedition can also leave someone injured. events.title: From Wood to Stone: Grow Your Civilization
events.summary: In the demo, you begin by laying the foundations of a wooden settlement. Build shelters, storage, workshops, and fences to give your people a place to live, store resources, and survive the night. Buildings are more than visual upgrades. They change your capacity for population, storage, repairs, and defense, giving the settlement strength to move into its next age. What you build first changes what remains after the next dawn. events.title: Eastern Journey - A Village's History Beyond Its Walls
events.summary: Protecting the flame means looking beyond the village as well as caring for what is inside it. In Eastern Journey, a feature in development for the full game, residents can set out along the road to the east. An expedition needs food and fuel. Travelers will be away from the settlement for a time, so choosing who goes and who stays matters. A decision on the road can also affect their journey home. Returning Reports Lift the Fog The whole map is not revealed at once. Returning travelers chart confirmed routes and discoveries, opening the way to further exploration. events.summary: Before the first night arrives, gather wood, prepare the flame, and create a place for your people to return to. Daytime is for preparation. Gather resources, secure food, and build your first structures. Night is when you decide what must be protected. When dawn arrives, the actions of your people and the changes in your settlement become part of its record. The warmth of timber Longhouses and wood workshops express the beginnings of civilization and the everyday lives of its residents. The strength of stone Stone archives, stone clinics, town walls, and bell towers represent a settlement’s power to withstand danger.
